results.title: Organizational Culture and Perceived Performance: Mediation of ...
results.content: This study aimed to investigate the effect of organizational culture on employee-perceived performance and whether this relationship is mediated by perceived organizational support and moderated by employee motivation. The results indicate that only goal culture, rule culture, affective organizational support perception, and identified motivation have a positive and significant effect on perceived performance. The literature review conducted above leads us to study the effect of organizational culture on perceived performance and whether this relationship is mediated by perceived organizational support and moderated by motivation. This study aimed to investigate the effect of organizational culture on employee-perceived performance and whether this relationship is mediated by the perception of organizational support and moderated by employee motivation. Although this study makes a significant contribution to understanding the relationship between organizational culture, perceived organizational support, motivation, and perceived performance, it is essential to acknowledge several limitations that may have influenced the results obtained and that should be considered in future research.
